subject: Getting plyr binding functionality from dplyr

messages.author: e3fc8587db796618
messages.subject: Getting plyr binding functionality from dplyr
parts:
Hadley, one functionality I've used a lot in plyr has been the automated binds in ddply.  This doesn't seem to be possible in dplyr without applying bind and then adding the grouping variable separately.
How can I replicate u2 below without going to step u3b, which seems to be a lot messier ?

> u1=data.frame(var1=runif(100),var2=runif(100),fac=rep(c("A","B"),100))
> zfunc<-function(x) { melt(cor(x[,c("var1","var2")])) }
> u2=ddply(u1,.(fac),zfunc)
> u2
  fac Var1 Var2       value
1   A var1 var1  1.00000000
2   A var2 var1 -0.27555249
3   A var1 var2 -0.27555249
4   A var2 var2  1.00000000
5   B var1 var1  1.00000000
6   B var2 var1  0.06440629
7   B var1 var2  0.06440629
8   B var2 var2  1.00000000
> u3=do(group_by(u1,fac),zfunc)
> u3
[[1]]
  Var1 Var2      value
1 var1 var1  1.0000000
2 var2 var1 -0.2755525
3 var1 var2 -0.2755525
4 var2 var2  1.0000000

[[2]]
  Var1 Var2      value
1 var1 var1 1.00000000
2 var2 var1 0.06440629
3 var1 var2 0.06440629
4 var2 var2 1.00000000

> u3b=do(group_by(u1,fac),function(x){ z1=zfunc(x); z1$fac=x[1,"fac"]; z1 } )
> do.call(rbind,u3b)
  Var1 Var2       value fac
1 var1 var1  1.00000000   A
2 var2 var1 -0.27555249   A
3 var1 var2 -0.27555249   A
4 var2 var2  1.00000000   A
5 var1 var1  1.00000000   B
6 var2 var1  0.06440629   B
7 var1 var2  0.06440629   B
8 var2 var2  1.00000000   B

How can I replicate u2 below without going to step u3b, which seems to be a lot messier ?

do() is still a work in progress. I think in the next release of dplyr, you'll get the result you'll get what you want with just

do(group_by(u1, fac), zfunc)
